title: How does a river change the land?
question: Where does water wear away the most land?
steps: Press and hold the cloud over the mountain: it rains while you hold it.
The water runs down the mountain, round the bend and out to the sea. Watch where the land is worn away and where sand piles up.
Use the button at the bottom left to make the land gentle or steep.
observe: On steep land the water runs fast and cuts deep into the land. On gentle land the water slows down and drops its sand. In a bend the outer bank is worn away and sand piles up on the inside.

terms.name: Erosion
terms.description: Running water wearing away soil and stones.

terms.name: Deposition
terms.description: Water putting down the soil and sand it carried, so they pile up.

terms.name: Sand bar
terms.description: Low land made of sand the river put down.

law.equation: fast water cuts, slow water piles up
law.title: What running water does
law.description: Running water wears the land away (erosion), carries the soil and sand, and puts them down where it slows (deposition). On steep land the water is fast and cuts a lot; on gentle land it is slow and piles a lot up. A bend is cut on its outer side and piles sand on its inner side.

tip: Press and hold the cloud with one finger: it rains, and it stops when you let go. Several presses add up. Start over puts the land back.
tip_short: Hold the cloud to make rain

predict.question: Where does water wear away the most land?
predict.reason: On steep land the water rushes down. So it wears away a lot of land.
predict.bridge: Make it rain and see for yourself!

stages.text: Rain on the steep mountain and cut a new way for the blocked river!
stages.say: On steep land the water rushes down and cuts deep into the land. That is how valleys and river channels are made.
stages.miss: Hold it longer to make more rain!

stages.text: Pile up a sand bar by the sea at the river's end, where a turtle can lay eggs!
stages.say: When the water reaches flat land, it slows down. Then it puts down the sand it carried. Sand piles up at the river's end and makes a sand bar.
stages.miss: More rain to carry the sand!

stages.text: Wear away the outer bank of the bend and get the piece out!
stages.say: In a bend the water on the outside runs faster and wears the bank away. On the inside the water is slow, so sand piles up.
stages.win: The bank wore away! The piece!
stages.miss: More rain to wear the outside!

story.keeper: This river used to run from the mountain to the sea. On the night of the big thump, the earth fell down and blocked it…
story.clue: That thump again? …Oh, there's a piece buried in the bank on the outside of the bend!
story.map_clue: At the mouth of the valley, where the river winds!

kid.intro: This is the river lab. Running water wears away soil and stones and carries them along. Water wearing the land away like this is called **erosion**.

intro_more.text: When the water slows down, it puts down the soil and sand it carried. Piling up like this is called **deposition**.

kid.title: Hold the cloud and make it rain!
kid.say: On steep land the water rushes and cuts deep into the land. On gentle land the water slows down and sand piles up.
kid.tip: Hold the cloud to make it rain.

note.law: Fast water wears the land away and slow water piles sand up.
note.learn: Fast water wears the ground away and slow water drops its sand. Where a river bends, the outside bank is worn away and sand builds up on the inside.
